text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Delegates attending the national agricultural round-table conference agreed on Saturday on a 15-point "initial summary" asking the cabinet to urgently resolve the agriculture crisis. Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy said that the round-table will meet again in September.
- The Constitutional Court will rule on Tuesday on proposals objecting to the conflict of interest law.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The Smallholders top both polls published in this paper and Nepszava. The Socialists and the Young Democrats compete for second place, but have at least double the support of the fourth place Free Democrats. Three parliamentary parties would have trouble achieving the 5 percent threshold for entry into Parliament if elections were held today.
- Vladimir Dlouhy, the Czech Minister of Industry and Trade, will visit Budapest today.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Supreme Court is expected to pass a ruling today on a lawsuit arising from conflicts within the Christian Democratic Party.

- Gabor Bagi, deputy state secretary for foreign affairs, conferred with Juray Migas, political director general at the Slovak Ministry in Bratislava on Friday, regarding implementation of the basic treaty. (Sat.)
- Representatives of the Hungarian and Romanian education ministries have initiated an intergovernmental agreement providing for the mutual recognition of diplomas and scientific titles.
- The average number of unemployed people was 372,000 in the first quarter.
- The Saturday AGM of Csopak Rt. decided to increase the firm's equity by 250 million forints to 2.45 billion forints and agreed to pay a 10 percent dividend.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- President Milan Kucan of Slovenia and his wife will pay an official visit to Hungary on April 29. (Sat.)
- Customs guards seized 2.1 million forints worth of cigarettes at the Nagylak border station between Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The National Bank of Hungary decided to decrease the one-month repo rate by 0.25 percent to 21.25 percent as of Saturday.
- The AGM of the chemical giant BorsodChem voted to pay 120 forints in dividends per share.
- The plastics company Graboplast Rt. recorded a pre-tax profit of HUF 1.6 billion in 1996, up from HUF 599 million a year earlier.
- Bayernwerk AG of Germany is negotiating with the State Privatisation and Holding Co. on buying the Pecsi Eromu power plant.
- The AGM of the brewery Soproni Sorgyar decided on Friday to merge the company with another brewery, Martfui Sorgyar, effective April 30.
- The food processing company Globus' AGM decided on Friday to pay a 12 percent dividend.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The broadcast company Antenna Hungaria will shortly issue bonds in order to raise the additional 1.5 billion forints needed to carry out the developments required by the media law.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
